Market‑Entry Sequence ### Phase 0 – Preparation (Months 1–3) - Finalize product version for U.S. and German regulatory dossiers. - Build a *clinical trial plan* that satisfies both FDA and KBV requirements (e.g., a single RCT with sub‑analyses). - Engage a **U.S. reimbursement consultant** to map potential CMS/Medicare pathways (e.g., “Coverage with Evidence Development” or “Specialty Drug” analogues for digital therapeutics). ### Phase 1 – U.S. Launch (Months 4–12) | Milestone | Target | |-----------|--------| | FDA clearance | 6–9 months after submission | | Pilot with early‑adopter clinicians (e.g., sleep clinics, primary care) | 3–6 months | | CMS/Medicare coverage determination | 9–12 months | | Private insurer pilots | 10–12 months | **Why U.S. first?** - **Regulatory speed**: FDA SaMD clearance is typically faster than German DiGA approval. - **Reimbursement momentum**: CMS has begun pilot programs for digital therapeutics (e.g., “Digital Health Innovation Center”); early success can create a *reference case* for Germany. - **Data generation**: U.S. evidence will satisfy the clinical data requirement for the German dossier. ### Phase 2 – German Entry (Months 13–24) | Milestone | Target | |-----------|--------| | BfArM DiGA approval | 12–15 months | | KBV reimbursement application | 15–18 months | | Negotiation with statutory insurers (GKV) | 18–21 months | | Market launch in Germany | 24 months | **Why not simultaneous?** - **Regulatory parallelism**: While the U.S. FDA is reviewing, German regulators can process the DiGA dossier;
